kubernetes-cka-s1.1-04.reason: weak_card (name giveaway). Dropping both flagged 1.1 cards would leave 8, so this one gets the verifier's Immediate-default replacement, shortened for length balance. Page: 'When unset, Immediate mode is used by default ... binding and dynamic provisioning occurs once the PersistentVolumeClaim is created.' (final: fixed) (shortened to fit a 195 by 422 screen)
kubernetes-cka-s1.1-04.statement: With no volumeBindingMode in its StorageClass, a new PVC is bound or provisioned before any Pod uses it.
kubernetes-cka-s1.1-04.explanation: An unset volumeBindingMode means Immediate: binding and dynamic provisioning happen once the PVC is created. On topology-constrained storage this ignores Pod scheduling needs and can leave Pods unschedulable.

kubernetes-cka-s1.1-07.reason: tell: removes 'the control plane' as the actor (7T/0F pattern). Same fact, same answer. Page: 'a PersistentVolumeClaim without an explicitly defined storageClassName will be created using the most recently created default StorageClass.' (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s1.1-07.statement: With several default StorageClasses, a PVC omitting storageClassName gets the newest one.
kubernetes-cka-s1.1-07.explanation: When more than one class carries the is-default-class annotation, claims that name no class use the newest of those default classes.

kubernetes-cka-s1.2-02.reason: tell: removes 'the control plane' actor. Same fact, same answer. The explanation now adds context instead of restating the statement (verifier note). Page: 'the user will always get at least what they asked for, but the volume may be in excess of what was requested. Once bound, PersistentVolumeClaim binds are exclusive.' (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s1.2-02.statement: A PersistentVolumeClaim can bind to a matching PersistentVolume larger than the claim's request.
kubernetes-cka-s1.2-02.explanation: The binder gives a claim at least what it asked for, possibly a larger PV, and the binding is exclusive, so the extra capacity stays with that one claim.

kubernetes-cka-s1.2-06.reason: source_problem: moves from Go controller source to the v1.35 docs. Reworded as the verifier suggested, which also removes 'the control plane' tell. Page: 'PV removal is postponed until the PV is no longer bound to a PVC' and 'a PV is protected when the PV's status is Terminating and the Finalizers list includes kubernetes.io/pv-protection'. (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s1.2-06.statement: Deleting a PersistentVolume still bound to a PVC leaves it Terminating until that binding ends.
kubernetes-cka-s1.2-06.explanation: The kubernetes.io/pv-protection finalizer postpones PV removal while the PV is bound to a PVC, so the PV shows Terminating in the meantime.

kubernetes-cka-s1.2-10.reason: weak_card (near-copy of the warning, hedge 'can'). Dropping both 1.2-08 and 1.2-10 would leave 8 cards and 3T/5F, so this one gets the verifier's concrete-situation replacement, reworded without 'control plane' and shortened. Page: 'If you edit the capacity of a PersistentVolume, and then edit the .spec of a matching PersistentVolumeClaim ... then no storage resize happens.' (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s1.2-10.statement: Raising a bound PV's capacity by hand, then its PVC's request to match, leaves the volume at its old size.
kubernetes-cka-s1.2-10.explanation: Kubernetes sees matching PV and PVC sizes and concludes the volume was already grown by hand, so no resize runs. To expand a bound volume, edit only the PVC.

kubernetes-cka-s2.1-02.reason: weak_card (kube-node-lease gives the answer away). Three True cards were flagged in 2.1 and only one could be dropped, so this one gets the verifier's replacement. Page: 'The kubelet updates the node's .status either when there is change in status or if there has been no update for a configured interval ... much longer ...' and 'Lease updates occur independently from updates to the Node's .status.' The explanation names default intervals because the gap depends on configuration. (final: fixed)
kubernetes-cka-s2.1-02.statement: By default, the kubelet renews its node Lease far more often than it rewrites an unchanged Node .status.
kubernetes-cka-s2.1-02.explanation: Leases are lightweight heartbeats. With default intervals, the kubelet writes .status only on a change or after a much longer interval, which cuts API load in large clusters.

kubernetes-cka-s2.1-09.reason: weak_card (systemctl truism, LNX overlap). Kept as a rewrite because the section has to stay at 9 or more cards; uses the verifier's replacement. Page: 'kubeadm ships with configuration for how systemd should run the kubelet ... written to /usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf and is used by systemd.' (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s2.1-09.statement: In a kubeadm cluster, systemd runs the kubelet as a host service rather than as a static Pod.
kubernetes-cka-s2.1-09.explanation: The kubeadm package installs a systemd drop-in for the kubelet at /usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf, so systemd, not the kubelet's own manifest directory, starts and restarts it.

The statement is lengthened slightly ('an edit to') for 2.2 length balance; fact and answer are unchanged. (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s2.2-01.statement: The kubelet recreates a control-plane static Pod when an edit to its manifest changes the container image.
kubernetes-cka-s2.2-01.explanation: Updating a file in /etc/kubernetes/manifests tells the kubelet to restart that component's static Pod with the new specification.

kubernetes-cka-s2.2-04.reason: source_problem: the Components page does not name the Deployment controller. (final: fixed)
kubernetes-cka-s2.2-04.statement: While every kube-controller-manager instance is down, a newly created Deployment still gets a ReplicaSet.
kubernetes-cka-s2.2-04.explanation: The Deployment controller runs inside kube-controller-manager, so the stored Deployment gets no ReplicaSet until an instance of that process runs again.
kubernetes-cka-s2.2-04.misconception: Deployment reconciliation survives a controller-manager outage.

kubernetes-cka-s2.3-01.statement: Current metrics-server releases collect node and Pod usage from each kubelet's `/metrics/resource` endpoint.
kubernetes-cka-s2.3-01.explanation: The kubelet serves summarized per-node stats on /metrics/resource, and metrics-server v0.6.0 and later scrape it on every node. Older releases used the /stats/summary endpoint.

kubernetes-cka-s2.3-02.reason: weak_card (the Deployment wording gave a second, giveaway reason). Section floor reached; verifier's DaemonSet replacement. Page: 'cAdvisor: Daemon for collecting, aggregating and exposing container metrics included in Kubelet.' (final: keep)

kubernetes-cka-s2.3-02.explanation: cAdvisor collection code is built into the kubelet, so the resource metrics pipeline needs no separately deployed cAdvisor workload on the nodes.
kubernetes-cka-s2.3-02.misconception: Container metrics come from a cAdvisor workload deployed on every node.

kubernetes-cka-s2.3-04.reason: weak_card (dangling 'it', unclear whose Pod). Section floor reached; verifier's replacement. Page: 'collected by the lightweight, short-term, in-memory metrics-server'. (final: keep)

kubernetes-cka-s2.3-04.explanation: The docs describe metrics-server as lightweight, short-term and in-memory. It keeps no history, so long-term usage data needs a full metrics pipeline.
kubernetes-cka-s2.3-04.misconception: metrics-server persists the samples it collects.

kubernetes-cka-s2.4-02.reason: weak_card (the field name gives the answer away; hedge 'lets'). kubernetes-cka-s2.4-02.statement: A `podLogsDir` on a filesystem separate from `/var` falls outside the kubelet's disk usage tracking.
kubernetes-cka-s2.4-02.explanation: The kubelet supports a custom podLogsDir on the same disk as /var. On a separate filesystem it does not track that usage, so logs there can fill it up unnoticed.

kubernetes-cka-s2.4-05.reason: duplicate of kubernetes-ckad-s3.3-04. Dropping it would take 2.4 to 8 cards after 2.4-10 goes, so it gets the verifier's alternative replacement. Kubernetes does not manage that log rotation.' (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s2.4-05.statement: The kubelet rotates log files that a static Pod component writes into a `/var/log` directory shared from the node.
kubernetes-cka-s2.4-05.explanation: Kubernetes does not manage rotation of logs that components write to a volume shared from the node. The node's OS or the deploy tooling has to rotate them.
kubernetes-cka-s2.4-05.misconception: Kubernetes rotates every log file a cluster component writes.

kubernetes-cka-s2.4-08.reason: weak_card ('node-level' gives away DaemonSet). Section floor reached; verifier's storage-cost replacement. kubernetes-cka-s2.4-08.statement: A streaming sidecar that copies an app's log file to its own stdout can double the node storage those logs use.
kubernetes-cka-s2.4-08.explanation: The app's file and the sidecar's stdout copy both sit on the node. For an app that writes a single file, the docs suggest /dev/stdout as its destination.

kubernetes-cka-s2.4-09.statement: A sidecar running a logging agent such as fluentd makes the logs it ships visible through `kubectl logs`.
kubernetes-cka-s2.4-09.explanation: An agent sidecar ships logs straight to its logging backend, outside the kubelet's control, so kubectl logs cannot show them. Read them in the backend.
kubernetes-cka-s2.4-09.misconception: Logs shipped by a sidecar agent also appear in kubectl logs.

kubernetes-cka-s2.5-09.explanation: The kubeadm docs warn, with no exception for any add-on, that the Pod network must not overlap any host network: problems are likely if it does.
kubernetes-cka-s2.5-09.misconception: Overlay encapsulation makes overlapping Pod and host ranges safe.

kubernetes-cka-s2.5-10.explanation: Source NAT may happen before or after NetworkPolicy processing, depending on network plugin, cloud provider and Service implementation, so an ipBlock rule may match a node or load balancer IP.

kubernetes-cka-s4.2-02.reason: source_problem: the container-runtimes page says most network implementations set ip_forward themselves. release-1.35 preflight code has addIPv4Checks -> FileContentCheck{Path: ipv4Forward, Content: '1'} (ipv4Forward = /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward in checks.go), run from InitNodeChecks and JoinNodeChecks. The explanation now gives the real reason it has to be set before init. (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s4.2-02.statement: Before `kubeadm init`, the administrator enables host IPv4 forwarding on a Linux node used for IPv4 Pod networking.
kubernetes-cka-s4.2-02.explanation: kubeadm init's preflight checks fail unless /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward is 1, and the Pod network add-on is installed only afterwards, so the administrator sets net.ipv4.ip_forward first.

kubernetes-cka-s4.2-10.reason: tell: removes 'automatically' (4F/1T pattern). Same fact, same answer. Page: 'The kubeadm reset command does not clean any iptables, nftables or IPVS rules applied to the host by kube-proxy.' (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s4.2-10.statement: `kubeadm reset` clears the iptables rules that kube-proxy installs on the node for Service traffic.
kubernetes-cka-s4.2-10.explanation: kubeadm reset leaves the host's kube-proxy traffic rules in place. An administrator performs any desired rule cleanup separately.
kubernetes-cka-s4.2-10.misconception: Resetting a kubeadm node also removes kube-proxy's iptables rules.

Statement and explanation are unchanged. (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s4.4-01.statement: By default, `helm install` applies new CRDs from `crds/` before creating an operator chart's custom resources.
kubernetes-cka-s4.4-01.explanation: Helm registers definitions from crds/ before submitting chart resources that use those newly defined kinds.

kubernetes-cka-s4.4-02.reason: tell: removes 'automatically'. Same fact, same answer. Page: 'There is no support at this time for upgrading or deleting CRDs using Helm.' (final: keep)
kubernetes-cka-s4.4-02.statement: During a chart upgrade, Helm upgrades the operator's CRDs stored in its `crds/` directory.
kubernetes-cka-s4.4-02.explanation: Helm leaves existing `crds/` definitions untouched during upgrades; an administrator manages their changes separately.
kubernetes-cka-s4.4-02.misconception: Helm manages CRD updates as part of chart upgrades.

kubernetes-cka-s4.4-03.explanation: kubectl has supported kustomization files since v1.14, so kubectl kustomize and kubectl apply -k work without a separate kustomize binary.

kubernetes-cka-s5.1-07.explanation: The control plane sets this immutable label with the namespace name as its value, so a NetworkPolicy can target one namespace without custom labels.
